title: Konrad Zuse's calculating space and nuclear detonation test

tellings.quote: He theorized that it would be possible to test this in extremely high entropy events such as for example the detonation of a nuclear bomb.

plain: The German computer pioneer Konrad Zuse, in his work Rechnender Raum ('Calculating Space'), proposed that the universe itself might work like a computer, and he thought this could be tested in 'extremely high entropy events', such as the explosion of a nuclear bomb. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this in his own summary, alongside an online essay called Nuking the Matrix. The idea is that if reality is a computation, a nuclear blast might strain it enough to show the seams.
